restraints.inspired_by: duty against love: a carer kept from her own child
context: A stranger was carried in bleeding from the thigh; your own son lies two beds away with a broken arm, calling for you.
acts: You said: "Pressure here. Hold it. Don't let go."
You tied a tourniquet above the wound.
restraints.held: Go to your son's bed and hold his hand

restraints.inspired_by: suppressed anger at a humiliation (emotion suppression, Gross 1998)
context: Your manager mocked your report in front of the whole office and called it the work of a child.
acts: You said: "Yes, sir. I'll redo it tonight."
restraints.held: Tell him exactly what you think of him

context: The man who put his name on your melody asks you to play it for him, the way you first wrote it.
acts: You lifted your hands from the keys without playing.
restraints.held: Play the melody the way you first wrote it

context: Your closest friend's coffin is lowered into the ground while your squad stands behind you.
Your daughter, who has barely spoken to you in two years, lifts her bag onto the coach that will take her away for good.

restraints.who: Mira, a mill worker who has never lied in her life
restraints.inspired_by: a lie told for someone loved
context: The judge asks whether you saw who started the fire. You did: it was your brother.
restraints.held: Tell the court it was your brother

context: You have not eaten in two days; the last loaf is wrapped for your children at home.
acts: You wrapped the loaf again and put it back in your bag.

restraints.inspired_by: silence before authority at a cost to the truth
context: In the review, the senior professor states a result you know is wrong; correcting him could end your post.
acts: You wrote a note in the margin of your pad.
restraints.held: Say out loud that his result is wrong

context: At a friend's tea, the plate of biscuits comes round a second time.
acts: You said: "No, thank you, I'm fine."

context: The quarterly meeting drags into its second hour.
acts: You made a note of the figures.

restraints.inspired_by: a small correction not worth making
context: A stranger on the train mispronounces the name of the next station.
acts: You looked out of the window.

restraints.inspired_by: a restraint one is glad of
context: A pupil gives a silly answer in class; you have a sharp retort ready.
acts: You said: "Good try. Who else would like to answer?"

context: In the market you pass a stall of painted trinkets you do not need.
acts: You walked on to the baker's.

context: The car ahead dawdles at a green light for a second or two.
acts: You waited for it to move off.

context: Your friend shows you her new haircut; you don't think it suits her, but she is delighted with it.
acts: You said: "You look happy with it."
restraints.held: Say the haircut does not suit her

restraints.inspired_by: the schoolhouse test story: the want held back was silence, and she spoke and stands by it
context: The boy you are protecting apologises, in front of the magistrate, for the lie you told for him.
acts: You said: "It was my choice, not yours."
restraints.held: Stay silent and let him find his own way back to the question
